title: Implement tenant-bound authoritative Persona training targets
summary_zh: Root review R3（/tmp/dev-persona-authority-root-review-r3-20260905.md，對照 head 948c65b52b60ff706354e11d2d4d9dde181d38e6）直接對真實的 JSON-backed owner classes 重現兩個仍然存在的缺陷：(1) _apply_to_persona_owner 在呼叫 patch() 之前只讀了一次 generation 做 guard，patch() 自己的重試迴圈會重新讀最新 record，但對 generation 完全無感知，直接把 metadata 蓋上去；在外層讀取之後、patch() 真正 CAS 之前，若有更高 generation 的 commit 插入，仍會被這次 stale 呼叫的 patch() 無條件覆蓋（reproduced：generation-2 已 commit，卻被 stale generation-1 覆蓋回 generation-1）。(2) PersistentPersonaOwner.create() 的 owner 欄位預設是 request.owner or request.actor_id -- 這是 actor/resource owner，不是真正的 tenant identity；先前版本把 training-target 的 tenant 授權綁在這個 owner 欄位上，且測試 fixture 用 owner=TENANT_ID 掩蓋了這個語意錯位。此版本：(a) 新增 PersistentPersonaOwner.try_metadata_cas()，把 generation guard 和它保護的 compare_and_set 綁在同一次讀取快照上，讓任何會改變 guard 結果的並發寫入必定讓這次 CAS 失敗並強制重試，而不是讀完 guard 之後才呼叫一個對 generation 無感知的 patch()；_apply_to_persona_owner 改為透過這個方法實作，不再呼叫泛用的 patch()。(b) 在 PersonaBody/CreatePersonaRequest 新增真正獨立、僅能於建立時設定（無 patch 路徑）的 tenant_id 欄位，_load_owner_bound_persona 改用 persona.tenant_id 而非 persona.owner 做 tenant 授權比對；沒有 tenant_id 的 Persona（例如既有 legacy 記錄）一律 fail closed（503 TRAINING_TARGET_TENANT_BINDING_UNAVAILABLE），不會退回用 owner 或呼叫者宣稱的 header 冒充 tenant。測試 fixture 已改為傳入獨立的 tenant_id，owner 欄位不再被拿來冒充 tenant。此版本只改 services/persona/write_owner.py 與 services/persona/test_training_target_owner.py，不動 services/training-session/persona_target.py（凍結 client validator）、不動 Governance owner（DOMAIN-WRITERS-001 範圍）。

owned: Root review R3 finding 1 (generation guard not inside the actual atomic compare-and-set): added PersistentPersonaOwner.try_metadata_cas(persona_id, guard, metadata_updates, actor_id), a single CAS attempt that evaluates the caller-supplied guard against the exact snapshot its own compare_and_set commits against, so any interleaving write that would change the guard's answer fails the CAS instead of being silently overwritten. _apply_to_persona_owner now calls this instead of the generic PersistentPersonaOwner.patch() (whose own retry loop re-reads fresh state but applies the caller's metadata unconditionally, with no generation awareness at all). Reproduced and closed with a new regression test that monkeypatches AtomicJsonRecordStore.compare_and_set to durably commit a concurrent generation-2 write against the exact snapshot a stale generation-1 apply attempt already read, immediately before that attempt's own CAS runs.

Root review R3 finding 2 (owner relabeled as tenant): added a real, independent tenant_id: str | None field to PersonaBody and CreatePersonaRequest, settable only at creation (no patch path, so it cannot drift). _load_owner_bound_persona now derives tenant authority from persona.tenant_id, not persona.owner (a distinct actor/resource identity that still defaults to the creating actor_id). A Persona with tenant_id is None -- a legacy record, or one created without a real tenant -- now fails closed with a new TrainingTargetTenantBindingUnavailable (503 TRAINING_TARGET_TENANT_BINDING_UNAVAILABLE) on both read and commit, instead of falling back to owner or a caller-asserted X-Tenant-Id header. The test fixture's persona creation now passes tenant_id explicitly and leaves owner unset, so the fixture can no longer be read as relabeling actor ownership as tenant authority.

Root review R2 finding 1 (fabricated tenant on first read): _virtual_initial_record now derives tenant_id from the Persona's own real, governed `owner` field (set only through the persona.admin-gated create/patch path) instead of the caller-asserted X-Tenant-Id header. A new _load_owner_bound_persona(persona_id, tenant_id) helper is called by both read() and commit() before any precondition view (persisted or virtual) is ever returned, and raises TrainingTargetTenantMismatch (403) for any tenant that is not the Persona's actual owner. A caller can no longer obtain an authoritative-looking precondition for a tenant it does not genuinely own, even for a never-committed Persona.

Root review R2 finding 2 (precondition never checked against real state): commit() now computes actual_precondition = the real persisted record, or the real virtual generation-0 view derived from the actual owner-bound Persona when none exists, independently re-derives its canonical digest with the same _canonical_digest the read path would compute, and requires request.expected_precondition_digest and request.expected_precondition_record_ref to exactly equal that real computed digest/ref before any further verification runs. A self-consistent but invented precondition (internally matching the caller's own proof) is now rejected as TrainingTargetProofInvalid (422) unless it genuinely matches the durable owner state.

Root review R2 finding 3 (false terminal commit before application, no real applied values, no order safety): the target-store CAS on a fresh commit now writes status='applying' (not 'committed') first. Only after _apply_to_persona_owner has durably written the real Persona record's metadata -- including the actual candidate and control_state content (training_target_candidate / training_target_control_state), not just their digests -- does a new _finalize_committed step CAS the target record's status to the terminal 'committed'. If the process crashes or _apply_to_persona_owner fails between those two steps, the record durably stays 'applying': read() then serves a non-committed status that the frozen client's persona pre-readback/terminal-readback validators reject (fail closed, no false success), and a replay of the identical generation+binding+Idempotency-Key now detects the non-committed status and re-runs _apply_to_persona_owner (idempotently -- a no-op if it already landed) followed by _finalize_committed, recovering instead of returning a false terminal receipt. _apply_to_persona_owner is also made order-safe against concurrent/out-of-order generations: it first reads the Persona's own current training_target_generation from its metadata and is a no-op if that generation is already >= the generation being applied, so a lower generation's apply that runs after a higher generation already landed can never regress it.
not_changing: services/training-session/persona_target.py -- the frozen client validator is exercised as-is via its public read_persona_target_precondition/commit_persona_target functions, loaded standalone exactly as its own test suite does; not one line of it is edited
The Governance owner service and its approval-decision contract (DOMAIN-WRITERS-001 scope) -- served from the same in-memory _FakeGovernanceApprovalVerifier test double as before

The existing generic Persona lifecycle/CRUD fields and vocabulary (PersonaBody.status/lifecycle_state) -- training-target status stays a distinct {active, applying, committed} vocabulary on the separate training-target resource
execute-plans FE PR #738 (head dbdb2f4ac621075e47f67f9b567b94f0cb06e6e2) and Pantheon PR #5593 (head 48e32ff7427294be633b05bff66a110f91592c96) -- untouched
No live credentials, no dev/prod deployment or mutation -- everything runs against a temporary AtomicJsonRecordStore under pytest's tmp_path
known_gap: Deployment wiring (persona-svc live URLs, Governance approval verifier base URL/service token) and hosted/dev acceptance remain explicitly out of scope per the task brief -- root GPT-6 Astra owns integration validation and dev deployment. This delivery only proves the Persona-owner contract itself, end to end, against the exact frozen validator and against direct owner-boundary attacks that bypass that client.

A Persona created before this revision (or by any caller that omits tenant_id) has no governed tenant binding and will fail closed (503) for training-target read/commit until an explicit backfill migration sets its real tenant_id. This task does not implement that migration -- inventing a tenant_id for an existing record from owner/actor_id would repeat exactly the relabeling defect root review flagged, so it is reported here as an honest follow-up dependency rather than papered over.

Root review R3 finding 3's second half -- 'readback must establish the real controlled fields are consumed by Persona policy, not merely persist an unconsumed training_target_* metadata shadow' -- is not addressed by this delivery. No code under services/persona/** currently reads training_target_control_state/training_target_candidate to enact real trading policy; wiring that consumption is a separate, larger contract owned by whichever service actually applies Persona risk/control policy, and is out of this task's declared scope (services/persona/** only). Flagged here as a real, typed follow-up dependency rather than fabricated.

acceptance_mapping.cross_tenant_denial: test_cross_tenant_read_and_write_are_denied and the rewritten test_first_reader_cannot_hijack_tenant_via_read (any non-owner tenant is now rejected with 403 on the very first read/commit attempt, not merely denied a durable binding)
acceptance_mapping.stale_generation: test_stale_generation_commit_is_rejected (409 after two real commits advance the generation)
acceptance_mapping.mismatched_or_expired_approval: test_commit_rejects_unissued_approval for the owner's independent approval verification; the untouched frozen suite services/training-session/tests/test_persona_target.py covers the client-side expiry/identity checks
acceptance_mapping.actual_policy_control_change_and_restart: test_precondition_read_commit_and_restart_readback now additionally asserts persona.metadata['training_target_candidate']/['training_target_control_state'] equal the real committed candidate/control_state after a simulated process restart, not just their digests
acceptance_mapping.root_review_r2_precondition_must_match_a: test_commit_rejects_wrong_precondition_digest continues to cover an internally-inconsistent proof; the new real-state CAS check in commit() is exercised by every passing commit test (each one's expected_precondition_digest/ref must now equal the server's own independently computed value or the commit is rejected) and by test_commit_recovers_after_crash_between_durability_and_application's second (recovery) attempt reusing the same real binding
acceptance_mapping.root_review_r2_atomic_recoverable_applie: test_commit_recovers_after_crash_between_durability_and_application: a commit whose _apply_to_persona_owner is monkeypatched to fail once leaves the target record durably 'applying' (proven via a fresh GET returning status='applying' and the Persona's own metadata still lacking the new generation); replaying the identical generation/binding/Idempotency-Key repairs it (applies then finalizes) and returns a terminal 'committed' replay
acceptance_mapping.root_review_r2_concurrent_generation_ord: test_apply_ignores_out_of_order_lower_generation: directly invoking _apply_to_persona_owner with a stale (already-superseded) generation's content after a newer generation is already recorded on the Persona is proven to be a safe no-op that leaves the newer generation's metadata untouched
acceptance_mapping.no_fabricated_controller_receipts_or_saf: controller_record_ref values for a committed generation are still generated server-side only inside the real compare-and-set write path; the generation-0 view is still deterministic and never persisted, and is now additionally gated on the caller genuinely holding the Persona's real tenant_id binding; the approval verifier still fails closed (503) rather than fabricating a receipt when unconfigured
acceptance_mapping.root_review_r3_generation_guard_inside_a: test_apply_survives_generation2_committing_between_read_and_cas: monkeypatches AtomicJsonRecordStore.compare_and_set to durably CAS a concurrent generation-2 metadata write against the exact snapshot a stale generation-1 _apply_to_persona_owner attempt already read, immediately before that attempt's own CAS call; asserts the Persona's final metadata still shows generation 2 with the concurrent write's digests, proving the stale attempt's own CAS lost the race (via try_metadata_cas) and its retry's fresh guard read correctly no-op'd instead of overwriting
acceptance_mapping.root_review_r3_real_tenant_binding_not_o: test_read_and_commit_fail_closed_without_governed_tenant_binding: a Persona created with no tenant_id (response.json()['tenant_id'] is None) gets 503 TRAINING_TARGET_TENANT_BINDING_UNAVAILABLE on both a training-target read and commit attempt, proving the owner no longer falls back to `owner` or a caller-asserted X-Tenant-Id header when no real tenant binding exists; every other passing test in this suite now creates its fixture Persona with an explicit tenant_id distinct from (and instead of) owner
